thread:
matt: quick alignment thread on the rerank API contract before I land the change. focusing on: presence/meaning of score fields, ordering behavior at cutoff, and how adapters should fall back when they can't provide normalized scores.
jess: good call. lay out the concrete rules and a tiny HTTP example and we can sign off. :+1:
matt: draft rules below, please flag anything risky: (1) introduce a new normalized field `rank_score` in [0,1] when available, (2) keep `score` for legacy, (3) sort by rank_score desc, tie-break by input index asc, (4) if rank_score missing -> treat as -inf for ranking but still return the item, (5) truncate by top_k after sorting (no tie expansion).
carol: agree. also add `original_index` on each result so clients can map results back to request order without guessing. and include `rank` (1-based) in response.
diego: implementation note: adapters must try to produce `rank_score`. If they can't, they should set `rank_score` omitted and leave `score` if available. adapters MUST NOT synthesize incorrect normalized values.
sam-qe: test matrix I'll add: missing rank_score, identical rank_score tie, different raw `score` vs `rank_score` order, top_k cutoff boundary. we should make expectations explicit.
matt: HTTP example I'd like to include in the spec. anyone object to this payload form?
carol: looks fine. include a short example response showing both fields present and one example where `rank_score` missing.
carol: ```http
POST /v2/rerank HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
Accept: application/json
X-Rerank-Spec: rerank-v2

{
  "query": "find best answers",
  "candidates": [
    {"id":"a","text":"first"},
    {"id":"b","text":"second"},
    {"id":"c","text":"third"}
  ],
  "top_k": 2
}
```
matt: example response:
carol: ```json
{
  "results": [
    {"id":"b","original_index":1,"score":3.2,"rank_score":0.88,"rank":1},
    {"id":"a","original_index":0,"score":1.1,"rank_score":0.75,"rank":2},
    {"id":"c","original_index":2,"score":0.9 /* rank_score omitted for this adapter */ }
  ]
}
```
jess: note: clients that only read `score` may see different ordering than `rank_score`. add a compatibility recommendation: new clients must sort using `rank_score` when present and fall back to `score` only if `rank_score` missing. we should mark `score` deprecated in the docs and indicate a migration window (90 days).
matt: agreed. we'll add a deprecation header in responses when `score` is relied on? is that feasible?
carol: we can return `X-Deprecation-Warning: score-deprecated; will be removed in 90d` on responses from hosted endpoints. private deployments may opt out.
diego: also add a small determinism rule: servers must return results in stable order for identical inputs (same candidate ordering and same scores). That helps e2e tests and rollouts.
sam-qe: for determinism tests I'll assert: identical inputs -> identical responses bit-for-bit (except timestamps/IDs). we should version the spec to make breaking changes explicit.
matt: bump to rerank-v2? current clients expect v1 semantics.
jess: yes. require clients to send `X-Rerank-Spec: rerank-v2` to opt-in. default behavior for requests without header remains v1 for 90 days. then switch default.
carol: perf note: computing rank_score is an extra CPU step (calibration). we'll add a runtime budget in the perf docs and expose a flag `global_calibration` for cross-request comparability (off by default).
diego: what about partial results: if adapter times out, should we return partial results? prefer deterministic failure: return 503 unless `allow_partial=true` is set in request. if `allow_partial` true then include `partial: true` in response and still include returned items with their original indexes.
jess: add an explicit field `partial` (boolean) at top-level response if partial. and a `reason` string when partial.
sam-qe: tests for partial: ensure `partial` set, items present, and ranking still follows rules for those items.
matt: good. documentation bullets I'll add: - rank_score: canonical, normalized [0,1], monotonic mapping of model output per response - score: legacy, provider-specific, deprecated - ordering: rank_score desc, input_index asc - cutoff: strict after sort - missing rank_score -> treated as -inf but item returned - original_index present - partial responses opt-in via allow_partial - explain opt-in only (explain omitted by default)
carol: explain: if `explain=true` we return `explanation` per item (string). limit size to 2kb and scrub for PII. default false.
diego: adapters: try produce `rank_score`, otherwise omit. log adapter reason when omitting for telemetry.
jess: QA and SDKs: SDKs should update to prefer `rank_score` and expose a helper that maps results back to input candidates using `original_index`. Add a small migration guide snippet.
matt: action items: (1) I'll update spec doc and include these examples (matt) (2) diego: add adapter telemetry when omitting rank_score (diego) (3) sam-qe: tests for ties, missing rank_score, partials, explain size (sam-qe) (4) jess: SDK updates and migration guide (jess) (5) carol: perf note in runtime docs (carol)
ci-bot: matt pushed branch rerank/contract-v2 -> CI started :github: 1789992222
jess: LGTM on the semantics. will review the PR diff tomorrow morning.
carol: will verify the perf budget and how runtime flags expose global_calibration.
diego: will stub the adapter fallback telemetry and add a feature flag to opt into `allow_partial`.
matt: thanks all. I'll open the PR link here when ready. closing this thread so it doesn't get noisy. :white_check_mark:
